newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-French steelmaker Usinor's 1996 profits fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French steelmaker Usinor's 1996 profits fall.

text.p: Europe's largest steelmaker Usinor Sacilor announced on Tuesday its 1996 profits had tumbled, hit by lower demand and weaker prices, and cut its full-year dividend.

But Usinor managed to slash its debt by nearly half to 6.5 billion francs ($1.1 billion) from 11.0 billion francs and forecast it would meet its goal of nearly eradicating its debt by the end of 1997.
The company, privatised in July 1995, said it hoped to improve earnings in 1997, helped by a rebound in demand and prices and a firm dollar.
"There should be a significant upturn in the second half of 1997 regarding earnings," Chairman Francis Mer told a news conference, saying the first half of the year was looking disappointing.

The steelmaker said net attributable profit in 1996 fell to 1.49 billion francs from a record 4.43 billion on turnover that dropped to 71.06 billion francs from 78.42 billion. On a like-for-like basis, turnover was down 8.6 percent.
Usinor cut its dividend to three francs per share from four francs, but that was less than the market feared. Some analysts had expected the dividend would be cut in half.
Usinor shares gained 3.61 percent to 87.55 francs at 1202 GMT, rising above the 86 franc privatisation price for the first time in many months.
Operating profit slumped to 2.5 billion francs from 8.0 billion, with stainless steel registering the sharpest fall.

Losses at troubled long products unit Unimetal totalled 600 million francs, unchanged from 1995. But Unimetal is expected to cut its losses significantly in the first half of 1997 before turning a profit at the end of the year.

Sales were driven by flat carbon steels totalling 35.10 billion francs, down 7.6 percent. Sales of stainless steels and alloys were 16.5 percent lower at 16.33 billion francs, while turnover in speciality steels fell nine percent to 13.60 billion.

Usinor said demand was starting to rebound significantly in stainless and flat carbon products in Europe. "Although price charges are still low for the first quarter, some improvement can be seen, specifically in galvanised products," it said.
But it cautioned while volumes were up, "average prices, at least for the first half, should be lower than those of 1996".
Mer said annual contract negotiations with clients, notably in the car industry, resulted in lower prices.
But with inventories brought down and a firm dollar, steel prices could rise in the second half of the year, he said.
When it was privatised Usinor said it would strive to erase its debt by the end of 1997. Last autumn, it forecast it would have only a few billion francs of debt at the end of this year.
Finance director Robert Hudry told Reuters Financial Television that Usinor would meet that target provided it made no major acquisition.

Moody's Investors Service has said Usinor may have trouble meeting its debt goals if it acquires or takes a stake in Corporacion Siderurgical Integral of Spain (CSI). Usinor has said it was interested in the Spanish company, which is being privatised. ($ = 5.748 French Francs)
